_note: REPAIRS, REMOTE: the landing beacons. Written by Jessica 2026-10-14 on his 'make them unique', over Eliza's
remote copy of 07a. Structure unchanged: three repairs in ANY ORDER behind one counted objective, civilians
on first approach, recap on stage 100. Each repair sets its own stage in whatever order, so no journal line
Why it is remote, in the fiction: the beacons send the supply ships past, and any tech the crew could call is on one of them.
The beacon model is lit and blinking whatever state it is in, so no fault says 'dark': each is wrong, not off.
No say on the group: members fire in any order, so a line on one of them would not be the last. The closing call is recapSay (Eliza's field, 0537c08, off his play: nothing played at the end).
MODEL NOT ON THE APPROVED LIST, his eye first: Beacon01 (vanilla outpost beacon, STANDS, 4.9 m, measured
2026-10-14). It is the beacon players build for their own outposts, which is why it reads as somebody's pad.
recap: The crew at the <Place> had supply ships flying straight past them. I got all three landing beacons broadcasting properly, so the supply runs can land again.
recapSay: All three beacons are right, and the next ship's already answered the signal.

place._theme: Peopled, so somebody is there to own the pad. Keeps the base's own exclusions (no natural sites, no caves).
place._remote: REMOTE (place.remote), made 2026-10-14 by Eliza from 07a's structure on his plan; story and words rewritten by Jessica the same morning, so nothing here is a placeholder any more. LocTypeTest excluded as the remote base does.

prose.name: Repairs: Landing Beacons on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The crew at the <Place> have three landing beacons that aren't working right, and supply ships keep flying past. Any tech they could call is on one of those ships, so I'm going.

beats.objective: Fix the landing beacons at the <Place>

message.title: Misconfigured Landing Beacon
message.text: Still broadcasting the last owners' landing code.

beats.journal: Some of the crew were standing round this one when I got there. It was still broadcasting the last owners' landing code. I cleared it and loaded the crew's.
beats.name: Misconfigured Landing Beacon

message.title: Weak Landing Beacon
message.text: The antenna feed is cracked. Somebody has tried to tape it and given up.

beats.journal: This beacon's antenna feed was cracked, so it only reached a few hundred metres. Somebody had tried to tape it and given up. I patched it and it's carrying again.
beats.name: Weak Landing Beacon

message.title: Looping Landing Beacon
message.text: Repeating one burst over and over. Someone has pulled the reset twice and left the cover off.

beats.journal: A power surge had left this beacon repeating one burst over and over. Someone had pulled the reset twice and left the cover off. I reset it and it's back on its proper cycle.
beats.name: Looping Landing Beacon

broadcast: Our landing beacons aren't working right, and the supply ships keep flying past. Our tech's on one of them. Fix the beacons and the next ship might actually land.
_speech: Radio rules: no names, no places. Voice is ElevenLabs' 'Killian' (Irish, calm), NOT yet heard in game (voices.md); his ear decides.

approach._approach: His fact 2026-10-11: LocTypeOE_NonHostile POIs mostly have nobody unless a quest is there, so the crew the briefing names must be placed. Civilians appear round the first beacon on first approach.

_wording: 2026-10-27, his 'I know i'll be paid': the pay promise is gone; the line says why the job matters.
